summary: The lockout lands as a rework, not a bolt-on: the shared repo-kind classifier (locked_repo_path) replaces the hook's private product_path with a compatibility shim; the approved-plan write allowance is removed cleanly along with its recording path; the degraded window reuses the quickfix ledger/claim/budget machinery with a required reason; the guard's quote-aware syntax scanner is the correct fix (metachars inside quotes pass, active syntax denies) and the final hardening also catches env-var-laundered companion names. Live self-tests all held: the orchestrator's product edit was denied under an approved plan, a bare read-only status call passed with no stage open, a piped call refused, and the stale-grill and delta gates each correctly refused the orchestrator mid-story. The governance fork the worker resolved silently (quickfix/lite losing session-write rights) was surfaced to the human and confirmed; 0037 records the 0013/0031 amendment.

non_blocking_findings.summary: The worker demoted quickfix/lite from write-windows to tickets without the plan naming the 0013/0031 contradiction - caught in review, human-confirmed, recorded in 0037. The plan grill attested no contradiction; that attestation was wrong.
The first worker died mid-verify with the registry stuck 'running' (stale entry remains); detection was manual log-staleness observation. A liveness check on registry entries is follow-up material.

A parallel session committed a confirmed spec (windows-zero-setup) onto this story branch mid-stage; preserved on its own branch, reverted net-zero, scope-noted under 0023. One-worktree-per-story needs to mean one SESSION per checkout.

residual_risks: The lockout binds Claude-side tools; a session could still author product content into an exempt path and shell-move it - the opaque-write and bash-shape guards cover the known shapes, review culture covers invention.
Registry liveness: a dead worker can hold a phantom 'running' entry indefinitely.
